verdict.summary: CleanSpark remains a bitcoin miner with an undeveloped data-center option, and the current D grade correctly refuses to capitalize that option as if it were contracted AI revenue. Fiscal Q3 revenue fell 30.5% YoY to $138.0 million, while GAAP net loss reached $239.8 million and non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA was -$113.0 million. The quarter included $116.3 million of bitcoin fair-value losses, but core pressure is also visible in $85.5 million of cash cost of revenue against $138.0 million of mining revenue and $111.0 million of depreciation. Liquidity is not negligible: $202.6 million cash, $814.9 million of bitcoin and $761 million working capital. The counterweight is $1.78 billion of long-term debt and only about $0.8 billion of equity. Sandersville and other power sites could be converted for AI/HPC, but no customer, lease revenue or financed conversion appears in the quarter. Publication should therefore frame CLSK as a leveraged miner with asset reuse potential, not an AI landlord. The $12.66 activation remains mandatory.

business.overview:
CleanSpark currently earns substantially all reported revenue from bitcoin mining. BTC produced and realized price must cover electricity, hosting, fleet maintenance and heavy equipment depreciation; fiscal Q3 mining revenue was $138.0M against $85.5M cash cost of revenue before $111.0M depreciation. Cash and BTC totaled about $1.02B, still below $1.78B of long-term debt.

The AI transmission channel is reuse of powered land, interconnections and data-center shells for HPC. Sandersville is an option to lease or convert capacity, but the latest quarter reports no AI tenant, contracted rent or AI segment revenue. Conversion also requires cooling, network and reliability investment beyond mining infrastructure.

The model breaks if hashprice remains below fully loaded mining cost, BTC treasury value falls against debt, or HPC conversion demands capital before a bankable tenant is secured. Site megawatts do not guarantee suitable power quality or returns, and reporting-control weakness makes rapid project financing harder to evaluate.
business.moat: CleanSpark's potentially differentiated asset is a portfolio of energized sites and utility relationships assembled for mining. That can shorten time-to-power for HPC, but mining rigs are replaceable and the conversion moat is unproven until sites meet customer specifications and leases are signed.

earnings.beatNote: Fiscal Q3 2026 revenue was $138.0M, down 30.5% YoY from $198.6M. The $116.3M bitcoin fair-value loss was one component of a $239.8M GAAP net loss, equal to -$0.89 basic EPS. CleanSpark's non-GAAP measure moved from $377.7M a year earlier to -$113.0M of adjusted EBITDA. Cash cost of revenue was $85.5M and depreciation was $111.0M. Management gave no numerical revenue or EBITDA guidance. The caveat is that BTC fair-value accounting amplifies the loss, but excluding it still does not create positive adjusted EBITDA.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: CleanSpark reported 256,796,280 common shares outstanding at June 30. The 10-Q also disclosed 138,638,066 anti-dilutive securities: 103,941,450 convertible-note shares, 5,250,000 contingent preferred shares, 1,604,559 warrants, 1,931,334 options and 25,910,723 restricted awards. Adding them yields a 395.434M minimum potential-share sensitivity, not current GAAP diluted shares because conversion, contingency and treasury-stock rules apply. That overhang sits beside $1.78B long-term debt and makes the negative $762.5M liquid-treasury residual unsuitable for a positive per-share NAV claim.
